body.statement: For every \((\mathbf X_n,P_{\beta,n})\in\mathfrak M\), every realized bounded potential-outcome table and every pilot-measurable \(\delta_m\), \(E[\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}_{n,m}(\delta_m)\mid\mathbf Y_n,\mathbf X_n]=\boldsymbol\tau_n\) and \[R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)=d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)-(N/n)^2E_{S_m}d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta)+(N/n)^2E\{V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\delta_m,\beta)-V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta),\beta)\}.\] This identity remains exact under randomized ties and unequal \(\pi_{iq}\), a case not represented by the ordinary symmetric factorial estimator of Branson, Dasgupta, and Rubin.
body.justification: Exact centering isolates pilot opportunity cost from learned-action regret without symmetry assumptions.
body.gap: Horvitz and Thompson give fixed-design unbiasedness, while Branson, Dasgupta, and Rubin use symmetric factorial rerandomization; neither supplies this pilot-conditional pooled identity under a learned unequal-inclusion law.
body.consumer: It permits unbiased reuse of both waves in sequential factorial cycles whose learned acceptance rule is not label symmetric.
